topic: The Anterior Midcingulate Cortex (aMCC) and Willpower
title: Willpower Isn’t a Battery — What the aMCC Actually Does #Shorts
description:
Willpower is not a tiny battery that simply runs out. The anterior midcingulate cortex (aMCC) is part of a brain network that weighs effort, reward, discomfort, attention, and the body’s available resources when a goal gets hard.

The practical takeaway: make the next action smaller and obvious, remove friction, make progress visible, and connect effort to a meaningful reward. That can make persistence the rational next move.

#Willpower #Neuroscience #aMCC #Motivation #CognitiveControl #Psychology #Productivity #Shorts
